column3: “From defeating Amalek” is rendered “from the slaughter of the Amalekites.”
“Earth on his head” is rendered “dust,” and “bowed down” as “prostrated himself.”
“What was the word?” is rendered “How did things go?”
“The owners of the horses” is rendered “the horsemen,” and “overtook” as “pursued him closely.”
“He turned behind him” is rendered “he looked behind him.”
“Dizziness” (Hebrew הַשָּׁבָץ) is rendered “agony,” and “for all my life is still in me” as “because my life still lingers in me.” The meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “so also did.”
“A man, a sojourner” is rendered “an alien.”
“Draw near, fall on him” is rendered “Go, cut him down.”
“Lamented this lamentation” is rendered “chanted with this lament.”
The Hebrew has only “Bow”; NASB supplies “them” and “the song of” (“the song of the bow”). “Descendants of Judah” is rendered “sons of Judah.”
“The beauty” is rendered “Your beauty”; “beauty” may also mean “gazelle.”
“Fields of contributions” is rendered “fields of offerings”; the Hebrew is difficult.
